required_own_edits.source_excerpt: [F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] and [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]]: the noise coordinates are independent standard normals with even density, first and third moments zero, and second and fourth moments $1$ and $3$.
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: [F4] [[def-ip-isonormal-white-noise-experiment]] supplies independent standard-normal coordinates with normalized density $\varphi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-t^2/2}$ and covariance one. We use the scalar calculation of [[lem-standard-normal-fourth-moment]] with this supplied law, rather than invoke its AC-based law construction: $\varphi\prime(t)=-t\varphi(t)$, so integration by parts on $[-R,R]$ gives $\int t^2\varphi=[-t\varphi]_{-R}^R+\int\varphi$ and $\int t^4\varphi=[-t^3\varphi]_{-R}^R+3\int t^2\varphi$. The polynomial-Gaussian boundary terms vanish as $R\to\infty$; the nonnegative integrals increase to their full integrals. Supplied normalization therefore gives second and fourth moments $1$ and $3$; symmetry gives first and third moments zero. This supplied-law calculation uses no additional choice.
